riepilogo:
Lab «programma-memorizzato» is finished and checked in the browser. Mode B (von Neumann) is now fully written in place of the placeholder; mode A (ENIAC, from round 1) was QA'd and fixed.

Mode B, built on window.CpuGiocattolo:
- 32 memory cells: address, program label (ciclo, n, uno, somma…), decoded text and 8 coloured bits; cell 31 is labelled USCITA.
- A CPU block with PC, IR (opcode amber, address azure) and ACC, plus a strip for the three phases: prelievo, decodifica, esecuzione.
- Two bus lanes (indirizzi azure, dati green) with schematic taps to the CPU and the memory, and an azure PC cursor that glides over the memory.
- Packets travel along the bus: address PC→cell; instruction cell→IR; address from the IR's 5 address bits →cell; number cell→ACC or ACC→cell; output ACC→31 in pink; jump IR→PC.
- Controls: «Fase», «Istruzione», «▶ Esegui / ❚❚ Pausa / ▶ Continua / ▶ Esegui di nuovo», «↺ Da capo», and a speed slider (molto lenta … turbo; turbo skips the packets so a whole run takes about 3 s).
- Programs: Somma and Conto alla rovescia, plus «↶ Programma originale» when edited.
- Narration is in my own words (a richer decode step with what each opcode does). Manual steps show all three phases one after the other and announce them via ctx.annuncia; during a run a short line per instruction is shown.
- The punchline: at HALT, ctx.completa() is called and the narration offers «Apri la cella 11». The bit editor opens inline right under the clicked row, with bits grouped (opcode / address, or number), their place values, the cell read both as an instruction and as a number, and a reference line of the 8 opcodes. Switching on the bit worth 2 turns 5 into 7; the rerun prints 28 next to «Esecuzione precedente: 15», and a panel compares «ENIAC: giorni» with «Qui: 1,2 s · 1 cella».
- If any action interrupts an animation (rapid clicks, reset, mode change), the interrupted phase finishes instantly, so the state never breaks. ▶ pauses itself after 300 instructions without HALT, because an edited program can loop forever.
- Keyboard: one Tab stop for the grid (arrows, Home, End), Enter/Space to open, Esc closes and returns focus to the cell; aria labels throughout.

Mode A fixes:
- Below 620 px, unit names were hidden under the neon displays: units now use a two-row layout, three rows below 420 px.
- Knob discs were squashed (flex shrink).
- Durations now come from ctx.DURATA.
- An unverifiable claim was removed and the von Neumann credit reworded.

Logic: new pure helpers (etichetteCelle, disassembla, testoCella, descriviCella, gruppiBit, pesoBit, suggerisci, elencoCelle, celleDiverse, livello, nomeVelocita, pausaIstruzione, LIMITE_ISTRUZIONI). Speed durations follow the --pg-dur-* tokens. 23 Node tests cover all the helpers.

fatti.affermazione: ENIAC did 5,000 additions per second (mode A narration: «5.000 somme al secondo»).
fatti.fonte: Not re-searched by me: the shared WebSearch budget was used up. It matches the source-backed text of chapter js/capitoli/03-cavi.js («Eseguiva 5.000 addizioni al secondo»), which cites Computer History Museum, This Day in History: February 14, https://www.computerhistory.org/tdih/february/14/

fatti.affermazione: Setting up a new calculation on ENIAC took days (mode A «ENIAC vero: giorni»; mode B «ENIAC: giorni di cavi e manopole»). The unverified phrase about weeks of paper planning was removed.
fatti.fonte: Chapter 03-cavi.js: «Preparare un nuovo calcolo richiedeva uno o più giorni»; sources Haigh, Priestley, Rope, ENIAC in Action (MIT Press 2016), https://eniacinaction.com/ and CHM https://www.computerhistory.org/tdih/february/14/

fatti.affermazione: Mode label «A · ENIAC 1946»: ENIAC was presented to the public in mid-February 1946.

Mode label «B · Von Neumann 1945»: the First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC circulated on 30 June 1945, signed by von Neumann alone. The lab now says «descritta nel 1945 nel rapporto firmato da von Neumann».
fatti.fonte: Chapter 03-cavi.js; scan of the First Draft at https://archive.org/details/firstdraftofrepo00vonn

fatti.affermazione: ENIAC results were punched on IBM cards (mode A «Schede perforate», «viene perforato su una scheda»).
fatti.fonte: General knowledge (IBM card reader in, IBM card punch out); not re-checked in this session because the search budget was used up.

fatti.affermazione: The lab's CPU, programs and instruction counts: Somma prints 15 in 42 instructions; with n = 7 it prints 28 in 58; Conto prints 3, 2, 1, and with n = 7 prints 7…1.
fatti.fonte: js/lib/cpu-giocattolo.js, checked by test/programma-memorizzato.test.js and in the browser

verifiche:
Tests:
- node --test test/programma-memorizzato.test.js: 23/23 pass.
- node --test test/dati.test.js: «tutti i file caricati da index.html esistono» passes, «capitolo 3 · cavi» passes. 7 failures are in other agents' chapters (4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 13, 14); none mention my lab.

Browser, via scatta.js and two Playwright scripts of mine in the scratch folder (prova-b.js is the functional suite, foto.js captures mid-animation states):
- Screenshots looked at: mode A at 1440 and at 390 during re-wiring; mode A panel at 320; mode B at 1440 light, 1440 dark mid-flight, 390 with the editor open, 390 mid-flight, 320 with reduced motion and the editor open, 768, and the 1440 punchline state.
- Numeric overflow checks at 600, 820, 1024 and 1300 px.

What prova-b.js exercises (all OK at 1440 and 390; the run, punchline and keyboard checks also at 320 and with reduced motion):
- Run to HALT in turbo: prints 15 and the lab gets the «esplorato» mark.
- Open cell 11, which reloads it to 5, with focus on a bit; the bit worth 2 makes it 7; the rerun prints 28, the narration says «prima: 15» and «giorni», and «Programma originale» restores everything.
- 7 rapid clicks on Fase give exactly 2 instructions plus a fetch (PC 03); «Istruzione» finishes the instruction in progress.
- «Da capo» during a slow flight, a mode change while running (state kept, nothing runs in the background), and Esegui then Pausa.
- Keyboard: arrows, Home/End, a single Tab stop for the grid, Enter opens, Space toggles a bit, Esc closes and returns focus.
- Scrolled offscreen the run stops; it resumes when visible again.
- Changing HALT into JUMP 0 makes ▶ pause itself at 300 instructions.
- Mode A: rapid switching between problems ends with the correct wiring, and Somma punches 5.

Every run: no console errors, no horizontal overflow inside the lab, all text at least 13 px, all targets at least 40 px.

Bugs found and fixed during QA:
- The IR showed «[object HTMLSpanElement]».
- At 320 px the editor overflowed (an unbreakable opcode reference line).
- In mode A at narrow widths, unit names were hidden under the neon displays, and the knob discs were squashed.
- Highlight and flash colours overwrote each other.
- «✓ Decodifica» wrapped in its pill.
- Packets landed in the middle of a register instead of on its value.
- «1 istruzioni».
limiti:
- I could not run my own WebSearch: the shared budget for the turn was used up, and I did not work around it. The figures shown match the source-backed text of chapter 03-cavi.js. The «settimane di progetto» claim was removed. The punched-card output of ENIAC comes from general knowledge and should be re-checked if the integrator wants a source.
- Mode A is still the default view, so the reader sees the problem before the solution, even though the spec calls B the main mode. A's final message has a button that switches to B.
- At the default speed (veloce) a full Somma run with ▶ takes about 45 s. The narration suggests «turbo», which takes about 3 s.
- If the window is resized during a flight, the packet finishes on the old path; the next flight uses the new layout.
- Mode B reads ctx.DURATA, so its timing follows the tokens; the copy of the values used by the tests (DURATE) must change if the tokens change.
